title: Gracious Lord, Our Children See
description: Gracious Lord, Our Children See in Tonic Solfa to WATCHMAN, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 12, “Prayer for children”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WATCHMAN; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Gra-cious Lord, our child-ren see, By thy mer-cy we are free; But shall these, a-las! re-main Sub-jects still of Sa-tan's reign? Is-rael's young ones, when of old Pha-raoh threat-ened to with-hold; Then thy mes-sen-ger said, "No; Let the child-ren al-so go."

lines: Gracious Lord, our children see,
By thy mercy we are free;
But shall these, alas! remain
Subjects still of Satan's reign?
Israel's young ones, when of old
Pharaoh threatened to withhold;
Then thy messenger said, "No;
Let the children also go."
When the angel of the Lord
Drawing forth his dreadful sword,
Slew, with an avenging hand,
All the first-born of the land:
Then thy peoples' doors he passed,
Where the bloody sign was placed;
Hear us, now, upon our knees,
Plead the blood of Christ for these!
Lord we tremble, for we know
How the fierce malicious foe;
Wheeling round his watchful flight,
Keeps them ever in his sight:
Spread thy pinions, King of kings!
Hide them safe beneath thy wings;
Lest the rav'nous bird of prey
Stoop, and bear the brood away.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to WATCHMAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
